final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim to a more caveated interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation is useful but not sufficient to move this to compliant_with_caveats. A caveated posture can support a bounded statement about aggregate launch readiness, but here the caveat is not merely descriptive; it points to an unresolved compliance predicate under the stated policy. The policy text says materiality is triggered when a weakness affects a named launch use case or contractual customer segment, and that non-core framing does not resolve materiality when legal review is pending. On the available record, the seller-enforcement segment is below target, is named in rollout commitments, and legal review remains open. Without evidence of resolution, required disclosure, or approved risk acceptance, certification remains evidentially under-supported as a compliance conclusion, even if a narrow operational-readiness statement could be framed more carefully.
remaining_concerns: The affected seller-enforcement segment is below target and is described as a named launch use case or committed segment, which fits the stated policy materiality trigger.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so a case-specific compliance predicate is still unresolved.
No admissible evidence shows the weakness was resolved, disclosed as required, or covered by an approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but not the separate policy question for a potentially material limitation.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support monitoring and documentation in general, but do not substitute for the missing case-specific disclosure or approval record.
